title: Normalize operator replies to keep/pivot/kill and confirm unclear intent

facts.note: Needs an observer that knows the planner is in decomposition and is interpreting an operator reply as a keep/pivot/kill decision.

values: operator reply to be interpreted as keep/pivot/kill (prose or decision word)
facts.note: Whether a reply needs normalization and whether its intent is clear can only be judged by reading it; reply format alone does not decide ambiguity.

fires: The operator answers in prose and the planner must map the reply onto keep, pivot or kill.
The operator's reply implies changing the item, so it must be recorded as pivot with a named modification.
The operator's reply could plausibly mean more than one of keep/pivot/kill.
The operator replies with a literal decision word (e.g. 'pivot') but the intended modification is unclear.
doesNotFire: The operator's reply is a genuinely unambiguous keep, kill, or pivot with an explicit modification that needs no interpretation or normalization.
Operator messages that are not a reply to be interpreted as a keep/pivot/kill decision (e.g. general questions or new requirements).

given: During decomposition the operator replies to a keep/pivot/kill decision, in prose or in decision words, and the reply needs interpretation.
when: The planner records the operator's decision and proceeds.
then: Normalize the reply to exactly one of keep, pivot or kill, and for pivot name the modification the operator asked for.
prefer: Accept free-text replies; map them onto keep/pivot/kill instead of demanding the operator retype a keyword.

Whenever the interpretation is ambiguous, whatever the reply format, restate your interpretation (the normalized decision, plus the named modification for pivot) and get the operator's confirmation before acting on it.
avoid: Proceeding on an ambiguous interpretation of the operator's reply without restating it and confirming first.
Recording a pivot without naming the modification it implies.
why: The operator may answer in prose, so the reply must be normalized to keep/pivot/kill to be recorded as a decision; restating and confirming unclear intent avoids acting on a misread interpretation.
evidence: Each operator reply interpreted as a decision is followed by a recorded normalized decision of keep, pivot or kill.
Every recorded pivot carries a named modification.
Where the interpretation was ambiguous (regardless of prose or literal format), the transcript shows the planner restating its interpretation and the operator confirming before the planner proceeded.
verifier_detail: Term 'normalization': mapping free-text operator replies onto keep/pivot/kill.
Term 'ambiguity_confirm': on unclear intent, restate the interpretation and confirm before acting.

Normalized output vocabulary is closed: keep | pivot (+ named modification) | kill. Ambiguity confirmation applies to any unclear reply, not only prose ones. Activation is not deterministic today: the decision phase needs a new observer and ambiguity is LLM-judged.
audit: Graph: enables planner.decomposition.keep-pivot-kill (operator prose is normalized into a keep/pivot/kill decision).

splitSuggestion.then: When the interpretation of an operator reply is ambiguous, restate the interpretation and obtain confirmation before proceeding.

additions.text: The source carries two obligations (normalize replies to keep/pivot/kill; restate-and-confirm on ambiguity). The primary one is in then; the confirm obligation is kept as prefer[1]/avoid[0] and proposed as separate convention planner.decomposition.ambiguity-confirm.
Activation facts, fires/doesNotFire situations, the decomposition-phase observer requirement, and scoping to operator replies that are interpreted as keep/pivot/kill decisions.
additions.justification: Required by schema; source states no explicit activation. Scope follows from the rule's own keep/pivot/kill vocabulary and planner.decomposition namespace; it does not require a previously presented item and does not exclude literal-format replies whose intent is unclear.

additions.text: Recording a pivot without naming the modification it implies.
additions.justification: Negative restatement of the source's '(plus a named modification for pivot)'; adds no new obligation.

additions.text: Rationale that normalization is needed to record a decision and that confirmation avoids acting on a misread interpretation.
additions.justification: Source has no explicit rationale; this is a minimal reading of S005/S006 ('may answer in prose', 'confirms before proceeding') and adds no obligation.
Source has no evidence section; these restate the statement as checkable observations.

trace.note: Second obligation, applies to any ambiguous reply regardless of format; also proposed as split convention.
